# klms 0.2.1

## Install and update

- Add `klms update`, the `upgrade` alias, and `update --check`. Updates use the
  official stable release, verify its checksum and binary version, and update
  the invoked executable without requiring a KLMS session or downgrading.
- Use one candidate installer for bootstrap, source installs, and updates.
  Skill-path conflicts preserve the previous executable; ordinary binary
  replacement failures restore the previous skill.
- Test both release targets and smoke-test packaged archives and installation
  before publication. Release tags must match the binary version.

Users on 0.2.0 or earlier need to rerun the standalone installer once to gain
the update command.

## Correctness

- Reject incomplete HTTP byte ranges in direct downloads before publishing a file.
- Preserve supported Moodle/ISO dates and space-separated timestamps; reject
  malformed date suffixes instead of silently discarding times.
- Reject typed detail redirects that change the requested resource identity.
- Return successful JSON help and version results rather than usage errors.
- Canonicalize library reference aliases before storing edits and retractions.
- Retain fresh file validators even when downloaded bytes are unchanged, avoiding
  redundant downloads without duplicating blobs or reporting a false byte change.
- Keep bounded object-store reads inside the corpus module and preserve UTF-8
  text previews when their byte bound falls inside a character.
- Clarify that absence is recorded per complete collection observation, even
  when another part of a sync fails.

- Bound SSO responses and curation file/stdin reads while streaming.
- Reject malformed resource IDs and ambiguous table headers instead of returning
  unusable references or combining unrelated title/link columns.
- Reject curation on immutable blob references before writing and report malformed
  stored JSON as library corruption instead of empty data.
- Make file-validation traversal deterministic and simplify command coordination,
  library query rows, and skill installation internals without changing the public
  command grammar or JSON fields.

## Development checks

- Replace source-spelling supply-chain assertions with parsed workflow/policy
  checks and behavioral fixtures, including real bootstrap rejection of untrusted
  archives. The YAML parser and CI runner are pinned development tools.
- Run shared fixture self-tests once, keep private updater tests beside their
  implementation, and consolidate archive tests across both supported formats.

No Rust dependency updates, trust-exemption changes, JSON envelope version
change, or SQLite migration are required.
